en.title: Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing
en.author: Robert Robinson
stanzas:
O to grace how great a debtor
daily I'm constrained to be!
Let that grace now, like a fetter,
bind my wandering heart to thee.
Prone to wander, Lord, I feel it,
prone to leave the God I love;
here's my heart; O take and seal it;
seal it for thy courts above.

notes: Text is hymnary.org's representative text, the near-universal three-stanza hymnal form. It is not a subset of Robinson's poem: the Cyber Hymnal prints five original stanzas, and stanza 2 here splices the second half of Robinson's stanza 2 ("Here I raise my Ebenezer... safely to arrive at home") to the first half of his stanza 3 ("Jesus sought me when a stranger..."). His other two stanzas ("Sorrowing I shall be in spirit" and "O that day when freed from sinning") are almost never printed. Last line: this source reads "mount of God's unchanging love"; Trinity Hymnal has "mount of Thy unchanging love" and the Cyber Hymnal "Mount of Thy redeeming love" -- all three are in circulation, so expect the question. Lower-case line openings and typographic apostrophes are the source's. Key D confirmed by the hymnchords.net Trinity chart and by hymnary, which lists NETTLETON in D and E; chords follow that chart. VERIFIED 2026-08-02: matches hymnary's representative text (Glory to God, 2003) word for word. Cross-checked against UMH #400 (hymnsite.com), which confirms "hither by thy help I'm come" and the three-stanza form but reads "mine Ebenezer", "Let thy goodness, like a fetter" and "mount of thy redeeming love"; Timeless Truths prints a further-altered four-stanza version ("Here by Thy great help I've come", "Bind my yielded heart", a final stanza ending "In Thy presence I shall stand"). This file's reading is kept.
